items.title: Equivariant constructible derived category of complex varieties
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

items.title: Acyclic product fibers stabilize bounded constructible pullback Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:Y\to S$ be an algebraic map that is a
locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of
[[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]]
and
[[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]]:
$S$ and $Y$ are the analytic spaces of separated finite-type complex varieties,
$Y$ trivializes over charts $V$ of $S$ carrying the finite conical cochain
models of the second supplier as products $V\times F\to V$, and the nonempty
connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$ carries a finite deleted-boundary model.
Suppose the constant-sheaf cohomology of the fiber is $k$ in degree zero and
vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$: $H^0(F;k)=k$ and $H^j(F;k)=0$ for
$1\le j\le r$, computed by the finite model. Finally, in the setting the
pushforward of every bounded algebraically constructible complex considered
below again has bounded algebraically constructible cohomology, with the finite
models supplied by the two named lemmas. Then, for bounded algebraically
constructible complexes of $k$-sheaves:

1. for $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to
   $D^{\ge b+r+1}$;
2. pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ whenever
   $A\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$, $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ and $m\le b+r-a$;
3. if $a-b\le r$, then $f^*$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
   $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$;
4. if $a-b\le r$, then an object $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ lies in the image of
   $f^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ if and only if the counit
   $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ is an isomorphism; the image is closed under
   direct summands, and it is closed under extensions when the stronger bound
   $r\ge a-b+1$ holds;
5. no global tensor splitting $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is
   asserted: the comparison is local and genuine characteristic-class
   transgressions are preserved.
items.strategy:
1.1 **The local comparison and the fiber model.** Let $V\subseteq S$ be a product chart with trivialization $Y|_V\cong V\times F$ and projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$. By [F1] there is a natural comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B_V\simeq B_V\otimes_kC^*(F;k)$ for bounded $B_V\in D_c^b(V;k)$, compatible with restriction to smaller charts and carrying the adjunction unit to $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. By [F2] the chart and the fiber carry finite deleted-boundary models, so $C^*(F;k)$ is a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces whose cohomology is $k$ in degree zero, in the sense that the structure map $k\to C^*(F;k)$ identifies $k$ with $H^0$, and is zero in degrees $1\le j\le r$. The comparison is compatible with the global adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [F3] over the chart: restriction to $V$ is inverse image along the open inclusion, inverse image commutes with $f^*$, $Rf_*$ commutes with restriction to the open base for open inclusions by [F3] and [F8], and the unit is natural, so the restriction of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ to $V$ is the chart unit. [given, F1, F2, F3, F8]

2.1 **The cone bound.** Let $\tilde C:=\operatorname{Cone}(k\to C^*(F;k))$, a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces with $H^0(\tilde C)=0$ and $H^j(\tilde C)=H^j(C^*(F;k))=0$ for $1\le j\le r$; hence $H^j(\tilde C)=0$ for all $j\le r$. Now let $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$, so $H^p(B)=0$ for $p<b$. By [F7] the cohomology of $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ is the direct sum of the terms $H^p(B_V)\otimes_kH^q(\tilde C)$ with $p+q=n$, and a nonzero such term needs $p\ge b$ and $q\ge r+1$, hence $n\ge b+r+1$; therefore $H^n(B_V\otimes_k\tilde C)=0$ for $n\le b+r$. Since the unit of the chart comparison is $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$, its cone is $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ up to canonical isomorphism, so the cone of the chart unit lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$ on every chart. The charts cover $S$, the restriction of the global unit to each chart is the chart unit by step 1.1, and vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of a complex is a local condition [F6], so the cone of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$, which proves claim 1. [F1, F3, F6, F7, step 1.1]

3.1 **The Hom comparison.** Let $B\to Rf_*f^*B\to C\to B[1]$ be the distinguished triangle of the unit, with $C\in D^{\ge b+r+1}$ by step 2.1, and let $A\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$ and $m\le b+r-a$. By [F5], $C[m]\in D^{\ge b+r+1-m}$ and $C[m-1]\in D^{\ge b+r+2-m}$; since $m\le b+r-a$ gives $b+r+1-m>a$ and $b+r+2-m>a$, orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m])=0=\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m-1])$. The long exact Hom sequence of [F4] applied to the triangle, shifted by $[m]$, therefore shows that the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. Under the derived adjunction of [F3] this map corresponds to the composition with the unit, $u\mapsto\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$, whose adjoint is exactly pullback $u\mapsto f^*u$; since the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ carries $f^*u$ to $\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$ by naturality of the unit, the induced pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. This proves claim 2. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1]

3.2 **The image criterion.** Assume $a-b\le r$ and put $\Phi=f^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ and $\Psi=\tau^{\le a}\circ Rf_*$. For $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}\subseteq D^{\ge a+1}$ by step 2.1 and $b+r+1>a$, so the truncated unit $B\to\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$ is an isomorphism; its inverse gives $\Psi\Phi\cong\operatorname{id}$. Now let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$. Since $C\in D^{\ge b}$ and $Rf_*$ preserves lower bounds (a bounded-below complex can be resolved in degrees at least $b$ by [F4], and $f_*$ of a complex vanishing below $b$ vanishes below $b$), we get $Rf_*C\in D^{\ge b}(S;k)$, and by the setting $Rf_*C$ has bounded constructible cohomology; hence $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\gamma_C:\Phi\Psi C\to C$ be the composite of $\Phi(\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to Rf_*C)$ with the counit $\varepsilon_C:\Phi Rf_*C\to C$ of the adjunction. If $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism, then $C\cong\Phi(\Psi C)$ with $\Psi C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, so $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. Conversely, let $C=\Phi B=f^*B$ with $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Then $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$, and the truncation $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\to Rf_*f^*B$ factors, up to the canonical isomorphism $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\cong B$ supplied by the previous paragraph, as the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$; the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{f^*B}\circ f^*(\eta_B)=\operatorname{id}_{f^*B}$, together with exactness of $f^*$, therefore shows that $\gamma_{f^*B}$ is an isomorphism. Hence for $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ the counit $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism exactly when $C$ is a pullback, which is the first assertion of claim 4. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 **Full faithfulness.** If $a-b\le r$, then $0\le b+r-a$, so claim 2 with $m=0$ gives that $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B)$ is a bijection for all objects $A,B$ of $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Inverse image is exact and preserves the canonical t-structure and algebraic constructibility by [F3] and [F6], so $f^*$ maps $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ into $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$; a functor between categories that is bijective on all Hom sets is fully faithful, so claim 3 follows. [F3, F5, F6, step 3.1]

4.2 **Retracts.** Let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ be a direct summand of $\Phi B=f^*B$ for some $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, with maps $i:C\to\Phi B$ and $p:\Phi B\to C$ satisfying $pi=\operatorname{id}_C$. The counit $\gamma$ is a natural transformation $\Phi\Psi\to\operatorname{id}$; naturality in the form $u\circ\gamma_X=\gamma_Y\circ\Phi\Psi(u)$ for $u:X\to Y$, applied to $u=i$ and $u=p$, gives $p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=p\circ i\circ\gamma_C=\gamma_C$ and $\gamma_C\circ\Phi\Psi(p)=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}$. By step 3.2 the map $\gamma_{\Phi B}$ is an isomorphism. Define $\delta:=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i:C\to\Phi\Psi C$. Then $\delta\circ\gamma_C=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=\Phi\Psi(pi)=\operatorname{id}_{\Phi\Psi C}$ and $\gamma_C\circ\delta=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i=pi=\operatorname{id}_C$, using the two displayed identities. Hence $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism and, by step 3.2, $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$, which proves closure under direct summands. [step 3.2]

4.3 **Extensions under the strict bound.** Assume $r\ge a-b+1$ and let $C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ whose outer objects lie in the image: $C'=f^*B'$ and $C''=f^*B''$ with $B',B''\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\varphi:C''\to C'[1]$ be its connecting morphism. Because $1\le b+r-a$ by the strict bound, claim 2 applies with $A=B''\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$, $B=B'\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ and $m=1$; the isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(B'',B'[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*B'',f^*B'[1])$ being pullback along $f^*$, there is a unique $\bar\varphi:B''\to B'[1]$ with $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$. By TR1 the morphism $\bar\varphi$ is completed to a distinguished triangle $B'\to\bar B\to B''\to B'[1]$ in $D^b(S;k)$ ([F5]). The long exact cohomology sequence of this triangle and $B',B''\in D^{[b,a]}$ show $H^j(\bar B)=0$ for $j<b$ and for $j>a$: the exact segment $H^j(B')\to H^j(\bar B)\to H^j(B'')$ has zero outer terms in both ranges. By [F6] the cone $\bar B$ of a morphism of bounded algebraically constructible complexes is bounded and algebraically constructible, so $\bar B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Exactness of $f^*$ [F3] turns the triangle on $\bar\varphi$ into a distinguished triangle with connecting morphism $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$; two distinguished triangles with the same connecting morphism are isomorphic on their third objects, because TR2 and TR3 applied to the identity on the source and target of the connecting morphism give a morphism between the two triangles whose first two components are identities and hence, by the five-lemma applied to the long exact Hom sequences of [F4], an isomorphism on the third objects. Thus $C\cong f^*\bar B$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. This proves the extension-closure clause of claim 4; at the boundary $r=a-b$ the degree-one comparison $1\le b+r-a$ fails and the argument is deliberately not used. [F3, F4, F5, F6, step 3.2]

5.1 **Conclusion and the local nature of the comparison.** Step 2.1 proves the cone claim 1; step 3.1 proves the Hom comparison claim 2, step 4.1 full faithfulness claim 3, and steps 3.2, 4.2 and 4.3 the image criterion and the closure properties of claim 4. The comparison used in step 2.1 is the local product comparison on product charts, not a global splitting: no isomorphism $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted, and the argument uses only the cone of the unit and the degreewise vanishing of the fiber model, so nonzero characteristic-class transgressions of the bundle are preserved. The only choice-theoretic inputs are those recorded in [A1]. [given, A1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2, step 4.2, step 4.3] ∎

items.title: General linear frame spaces have the Stiefel cohomology gap
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $s\ge1$,
$n_i\ge1$ and $N_i\ge n_i+1$ for $1\le i\le s$, let $k$ be a field, and put
$$U_N=\prod_{i=1}^{s}\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad r_N=2\min_{i}(N_i-n_i),$$
where $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is the open set of
injective, equivalently full-rank, complex $N\times n$ matrices. Then:

1. each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to
   the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)=\{A\in\mathbb C^{N\times n}:A^*A=I_n\}$
   of orthonormal frames
   ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]]);
2. each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold and is
   homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the map
   $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ forgetting the last column is a
   numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a
   Hurewicz and a Serre fibration;
3. $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.

No claim is made about the cohomology of $U_N$ above degree $r_N$, and no
GL-equivariance of the retractions or trivializations below is asserted.
items.strategy: Construct the Gram–Schmidt deformation retraction and regular-value frame manifold, give complement-basis sphere-bundle charts, apply finite triangulation and path lifting, induct in the Serre sequence through the inclusive gap, handle finite products starting at one factor, and identify constant-sheaf and singular cohomology on metric ball-chart spaces. AC discharges the exact supplier choice hypotheses.

items.title: General linear Stiefel approximations stabilize bounded constructible Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $U_N$ has the right action $u\cdot g=u\circ g$ and the quotient uses
$(u,x)\cdot g=(ug,g^{-1}x)$. For the action nerve use the equivalent left
action $g\cdot(u,x)=(ug^{-1},gx)$, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$ and $B_N$ are points and $X_N=X$, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

The finite local comparisons do not assert a global tensor splitting for an
arbitrary bundle with fibre $U_N$, such as the comparison projections
$X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
items.strategy:
1.1 **The frame bundle and its nerve.** On a Grassmannian chart determined by an invertible $n\times n$ pivot minor, a frame is uniquely $\binom{I_n}{T}h$, with $h\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$ and $T$ the graph coordinates. These formulas and their inverses are regular, so they give algebraic principal-bundle charts for $U_N\to B_N$. In these charts the diagonal quotient is $V\times X$, with $(\binom{I}{T}h,x)$ mapping to $(T,hx)$, and the principal quotient $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ has section $(T,y)\mapsto(\binom{I}{T},y)$. The finitely many charts glue by the regular change-of-frame maps; they exhibit $X_N$ as a separated finite-type variety and $q_N$ as a principal $G$-bundle. Its action nerve is its Čech nerve, so [F5] applies. Projection to $X$ is equivariant for the left action specified in the Statement, and induces the simplicial map $p_N$. In degree $m$ this is a product projection $G^m\times U_N\times X\to G^m\times X$ with fibre $U_N$; its structure squares are Cartesian, since group action on the frame factor is invertible. [given, F1, F5, F6]

2.1 **The fiber is $r_N$-acyclic with finite models.** By [F2], $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$, and the product of Stiefel models supplies the bounded finite cochain model of the fiber with coefficient-field compatibility. By [F4] the base $G^m\times X$ carries the finite conical cochain models, so each levelwise projection of step 1.1 is a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting with $r_N$-acyclic fiber. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 **The simplicial unit bound.** For a map of these nerves, the levelwise direct images acquire simplicial structure by the canonical sheaf base-change maps followed by the source structure maps. The levelwise adjunction gives $p_N^*\dashv p_{N*}$, with exact inverse image. Evaluation of a simplicial injective at degree $m$ is injective: evaluation has an exact left adjoint, whose degree-$l$ term is the direct sum over operators $[m]\to[l]$ of their inverse images of the given sheaf. These sums and inverse images are exact. Thus a bounded-below simplicial injective replacement evaluates to an injective replacement at every level, and $(Rp_{N*}C)_m=Rp_{N,m*}C_m$. For $B\ge b$, [F3] and step 2.1 give that the cone of $B_m\to Rp_{N,m*}p_{N,m}^*B_m$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r_N+1}$ at every level. The same bound therefore holds for the simplicial unit cone in the bounded-below derived category; no augmentation of the action nerve to $X$ is used. [F3, F5, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The simplicial Hom comparison.** The simplicial category has the exact levelwise inverse image $p_N^*$ left adjoint to the levelwise direct image $Rp_{N*}$ and carries the canonical t-structure of [F7], whose aisles are defined cohomology-objectwise and hence are the levelwise aisles. With the cone bound of step 3.1 in place, the argument of [F3] — its Hom comparison, image criterion, full faithfulness and its retract and extension clauses — applies verbatim inside the simplicial bounded-below derived category, with its bounded full subcategory: for $A\in D^{\le a}$ and $B\in D^{\ge b}$ the long exact Hom sequence of the unit triangle and the orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ identify the pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m'])\to\operatorname{Hom}(p_N^*A,p_N^*B[m'])$ as an isomorphism for $m'\le b+r_N-a$; for $a-b\le r_N$ it is fully faithful on the full subcategory $D^{[b,a]}$; and on that interval an object lies in the image exactly when the truncated counit $p_N^*\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}C\to C$ is an isomorphism, the image being closed under retracts and under extensions when $r_N\ge a-b+1$. Every input of that argument is an input already verified here: the adjunction and levelwise model [F5], the cone bound of step 3.1, and the t-structure orthogonality [F7]. [F3, F5, F7, step 3.1]

5.1 **Descent and the functor $Q_N$.** Restricting the conclusion of step 4.1 to the full subcategory of Cartesian objects identified with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$ by [F5], the functor $p_N^*$ followed by descent is $Q_N$: for $F\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ the object $p_N^*F$ has Cartesian cohomology because $p_N$ is a simplicial map and the structure squares of $p_N^*$ are Cartesian by naturality of inverse image; descent produces $Q_N(F)\in D_c^b(X_N;k)$, and $q_N^*Q_N(F)\cong p_N^*F$ canonically. Hence, for $A\le a$, $B\ge b$ and $m\le b+r_N-a$, the isomorphisms of step 4.1 compose with the descent equivalence to give $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$, proving claim 1; the same composition proves claim 2 on intervals of width at most $r_N$. [F5, step 4.1]

6.1 **The image and Cartesian descent.** Necessity follows from $q_N^*Q_N(A)=\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_0$ at degree zero. Conversely suppose $H\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ and $q_N^*H\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ for $F\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)$. Let $C$ be the Cartesian simplicial pullback of $H$ to the principal-bundle nerve, and put $E=\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}C$ in the ambient simplicial category. It lies in $[b,a]$ because derived direct image preserves lower bounds. At every level $m$, Cartesianity identifies $C_m$ with the pullback of $C_0$, hence with $p_{N,m}^*\operatorname{pr}_{X,m}^*F$, where $\operatorname{pr}_{X,m}:G^m\times X\to X$ is projection. The levelwise image criterion [F3] therefore makes the truncated counit $p_N^*E\to C$ an isomorphism in every degree. Its naturality compares the structure maps of $p_N^*E$ with the Cartesian maps of $C$. Each $p_{N,m}$ is surjective and its structure squares are Cartesian, so its exact pullback reflects these quasi-isomorphisms; hence $E$ has Cartesian cohomology. Moreover $E_0\cong F$ by the truncated unit and $C_0\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, so it is algebraically constructible. Thus $E\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ and Čech descent gives $Q_N(E)\cong H$. Retracts and extensions under $r_N\ge a-b+1$ lift by the degree-zero and degree-one Hom comparisons of step 4.1; their cones and summands have bounded Cartesian constructible cohomology, and the same counit argument gives the image. This proves claim 3 without assuming that ordinary descent data automatically strictify. [F3, F5, F7, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 **Coherence and the trivial group.** The product $U_N\times U_M$ is a free smooth $G$-resolution in its own right. Its projections to $U_N$ and $U_M$ descend to $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$, locally trivial bundles with fibres $U_M$ and $U_N$. Their pullbacks are fully faithful on the stated intervals by [F3] and the bounds $r_M,r_N$. On the common principal bundle $U_N\times U_M\times X$, both pulled-back representatives have the canonical descent identification with the same pullback of $A$ from $X$; these identifications are compatible with the principal-bundle nerve maps, so [F5]'s descent equivalence yields a canonical isomorphism $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)\simeq\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$. Naturality is inherited from those same inverse-image and descent maps. On the triple product all comparisons identify the representatives with the same pullback of $A$, so their two compositions agree and the cocycle law follows. This compares objects and Hom maps in the common category, without equating the two different target categories or identifying the product with a larger frame space. If $G$ is trivial, take the point as its resolution; then $X_N=X$, the action nerve is constant at $X$, $r_N=\infty$ and $Q_N$ is the identity. This proves claims 4 and 5. [F1, F3, F5, step 5.1, step 6.1]

8.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 3.1 to 5.1 prove claims 1 and 2, step 6.1 claim 3, and step 7.1 claims 4 and 5. The comparison is used only on the nerve and through the finite local models: no global splitting of $Ra_{N*}a_N^*B$ is asserted, so genuine characteristic-class transgressions are preserved. AC enters only through [A1]. [given, A1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

items.title: Cartesian simplicial sheaves model actual equivariant derived Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness
of restriction to $X$ is asserted.
items.strategy:
1.1 **The ambient category and its Hom groups.** By [F1] the category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ is abelian with levelwise exactness, has enough injectives under AC via the coinduced objects $N_pI$, and its bounded derived category is actual with set-sized Hom groups computed by bounded-below injective replacements. This is the ambient category of the definition, with the ordinary shift and cone triangles of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]. [given, F1]

1.2 **Closure under the triangulated operations.** Shifts and isomorphisms preserve Cartesian cohomology and the constructibility of the degree-zero restriction because the structure maps of a shifted or isomorphic complex are the shifts or conjugates of the original structure maps. For a cone $C(f)$ of a morphism $f:A\to B$ of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, the structure maps of $C(f)$ are the cones of the levelwise structure maps, and exactness of simplicial inverse image identifies the structural comparison for $C(f)$ with the map of cones of the structural comparisons for $A$ and $B$. Those two comparisons are quasi-isomorphisms by Cartesianity, so their cone comparison is a quasi-isomorphism by the long exact cohomology sequences. Thus $C(f)$ has Cartesian cohomology. The degree-zero restriction $C(f)_0$ is the cone of $f_0$ between constructible complexes, and by the common-stratification closure of [F2] it is again constructible. Hence $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of the ambient bounded derived category. [F1, F2]

2.1 **Conservative restriction.** Let $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with $A_0\cong0$ in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. All cohomology sheaves of $A_0$ vanish, and by Cartesianity the structure morphism of $H^j(A)$ along the projection $d_0^p:Z_p\to Z_0=X$ identifies $H^j(A)_p$ with the pullback of $H^j(A_0)$ for every $p$, so every cohomology simplicial sheaf of $A$ vanishes. An object of the bounded derived category with vanishing cohomology objects is zero by [F2], so $A\cong0$. Restriction to $X$ is thus conservative. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

2.2 **The finite resolution triples.** Apply [F3] to the frame resolution of $G$: the simplicial map $p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is levelwise a locally trivial bundle with $r_N$-acyclic fiber, its induced pullback is compatible with the simplicial structure, and the locally split Čech descent of [F1] for the principal bundle $P_N\to X_N$ identifies the Cartesian-cohomology derived category of the nerve of $P_N$ with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$. Composing with $Q_N$ gives the identification of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory of $D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ in the stated range: an equivariant object $A$ corresponds to the triple $(Q_N(A),\ p_N^*A\cong q_N^*Q_N(A))$, and conversely a triple whose frame pullback comes from $X$ arises from an equivariant object. The bounded Hom comparison of [F3] is induced by pullback along $p_N$ and the descent equivalence, hence carries composition to composition; at $m=0$ it is a ring comparison $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ for objects in the interval, and retract closure is inherited from [F3]. [F1, F3, step 1.2]

2.3 **Idempotent completeness.** Let $e:K\to K$ be an idempotent endomorphism of a bounded object $K\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Form the telescope in the bounded-below derived category of all simplicial sheaves: let $S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}K$ be the countable sum with the shift map $1-\operatorname{shift}(e):S\to S$ sending the $j$-th summand to the $j$-th summand by $\mathrm{id}$ and to the $(j+1)$-st by $-e$, and let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-\operatorname{shift}(e))$. Countable coproducts in $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ exist levelwise and are exact, and the cone is levelwise, so $H^j(T)=\operatorname{colim}_j\bigl(H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}\cdots\bigr)=\operatorname{im}H^j(e)$: the colimit of an idempotent is its image, and because $H^j(e)$ is an idempotent endomorphism of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(K)$ its image is a direct summand. The image of an idempotent of a simplicial sheaf is again a simplicial sheaf, is bounded, is Cartesian because it is a summand of a Cartesian object, and restricts on $X$ to the image of the idempotent $H^j(e)_0$, a summand of a constructible sheaf and hence constructible of finite rank. Thus $T$ is an object of the bounded-below ambient derived category with bounded Cartesian constructible cohomology, and by truncation it defines an object of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. The first-summand inclusion $i:K\to T$ satisfies $ie=i$ by the telescope relations, and the map $S\to K$ with every component $e$ annihilates $1-\operatorname{shift}(e)$, so the triangle yields $p:T\to K$ with $pi=e$. Then $ip$ is an isomorphism on cohomology, hence by [F2] an isomorphism. Also $(ip)^2=i(pi)p=iep=ip$, since $ie=i$. An invertible idempotent is the identity, so $ip=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $pi=e$, splitting the idempotent inside $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Hence the category is idempotent complete. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

3.1 **Triangulated, locally small, conservative.** Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 exhibit the ambient category and its Hom groups, the triangulated structure of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, and conservativity of restriction; step 2.2 gives the finite resolution identification and the degree-zero ring and retract comparisons. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted or used. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2]

4.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 give the triangulated, locally small model with conservative restriction and the finite resolution comparisons; step 2.3 gives idempotent completeness. AC is consumed exactly as recorded in [A1]. [given, A1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 2.3] ∎

items.title: Constructible six functors, proper base change and normalized equivariant duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.
items.strategy:
1.1 **Smooth comparison and image preservation.** On each quasi-projective source piece over an affine target, [F4] factors the map as an open inclusion into its graph closure in $\mathbb P^n\times Y$, followed by proper projection. The open-inclusion smooth exchange of [F1] followed by proper base change gives smooth exchange for $Rf_*$ on this piece. A finite affine source cover and its intersections compute ordinary pushforward by finite open-cover derived descent [F4]; smooth inverse image is exact, so the piece comparisons give the canonical smooth exchange for the general map. The comparison respects composition because its maps are the ordinary units and base-change maps. Proper-support exchange is already in [F1]; smooth exchange for tensor, internal Hom and normalized duality follows locally by adjoining a contractible smooth ball to their finite cochain models. For a fixed frame resolution, write $D^N_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_{X_N}[-2s_N])$. Smooth orientation gives $q_N^*D^N_XQ_N(A)\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*D_XA_X$, since smooth orientation gives $q_N^*\omega_{X_N}=\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2s_N]$ and both dualizing shifts cancel the dimensions $u_N=g+s_N$. The smooth comparison for the square formed by $q_N$, $f_N$ and $\mathrm{id}_{U_N}\times f$, followed by the product projection to $f$, therefore gives $q_N^*Rf_{N*}Q_N(A)\cong\operatorname{pr}_Y^*Rf_*A_X$ and likewise for $Rf_{N!}$. Inverse image and tensor have this comparison directly; internal Hom has it by its smooth comparison; $f_N^!=D^N_Xf_N^*D^N_Y$ has it by duality. Thus every ordinary operation on the resolution representatives satisfies the frame-pullback image criterion [F3], with an ordinary bounded constructible object downstairs. Its unshifted cohomological amplitude equals the downstairs amplitude, because both $q_N^*$ and $\operatorname{pr}_X^*$ are exact and conservative. These are bounds independent of $N$. [F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 **Transport of operations and adjunctions.** For each fixed finite collection of inputs, outputs and adjunction maps, choose $N$ whose gap exceeds the widths of their unshifted ordinary amplitudes and the finitely many Hom comparison bounds. By step 1.1 all the ordinary resolution operations lie in the finite-resolution image, so [F3] transports them to $D^b_{G,c}$. On a common product resolution the smooth comparisons identify the two constructions canonically; their coherence gives the cocycle on triple products, hence independence of the choice of $N$. Every bounded input is treated this way; no decomposition of an object into its cohomology sheaves is assumed. The ordinary adjunction Hom bijections, their units and counits, transport through the fully faithful comparisons. Naturality and the triangle identities are equations of these maps and are reflected by a sufficiently large faithful comparison. This proves $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ and the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction on the actual bounded equivariant category. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **Coherence.** Composition of maps, identity comparisons, support localization, the projection formula, trace and Cartesian pasting are equations between morphisms built from unit and counit maps of the ordinary adjunctions. By [F1] these equations hold at the level of the resolution varieties, and naturality of the resolution comparisons plus their full faithfulness on the intervals means that an equation holding after transport to $X_N,Y_N$ holds in $D^b_{G,c}$; more precisely, the comparison functors are faithful on the relevant Hom groups by [F3], so the two sides of each coherence equation, which agree after transport, agree before it. Proper equality $Rf_!=Rf_*$ transfers from [F1] in the same way. This proves the first part of claim 2. [F1, F3, step 2.1]

3.2 **Normalization.** For a frame resolution $P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N$ with base $B_N$ and maps $a_{X_N}:X_N\to B_N$, $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ and $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$, put $u_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}U_N$, $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$ and $s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N=u_N-g$, and define the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G_{X_N}:=\omega_{X_N}\otimes_k a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}$, the inverse taken in the tensor category of bounded constructible sheaves on $B_N$; here $B_N$ is a smooth complex $s_N$-fold, so by [F2] its dualizing object is $\omega_{B_N}\simeq k_{B_N}[2s_N]$ and $a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}\simeq k_{X_N}[-2s_N]$. Transitivity of dualizing objects for the smooth maps $\operatorname{pr}_X$ of relative dimension $u_N$ and $q_N$ of relative dimension $g$ gives $\omega_{P_N}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2u_N]\simeq q_N^*\omega_{X_N}[2g]$, hence $q_N^*\omega_{X_N}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2s_N]$ and therefore $q_N^*\omega^G_{X_N}\simeq q_N^*\omega_{X_N}[-2s_N]\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X$: the normalization cancels exactly the base contribution, so $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary $\omega_X$ under the forgetful maps of [F3]. On a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$, complex orientation gives $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$ by [F2], and no extra shift survives because the normalization removes exactly the base contribution: this is the exclusion of the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift recorded in the Statement. This proves claim 3. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 **Dual exchange and pasting.** Verdier duality on the resolution varieties exchanges $Rf_*$ with $Rf_!$ and computes $f^!$ by [F2], and the ordinary coherent exchange identities of [F1] dualize into the extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$; transporting through the normalized comparison of step 3.2 and the fully faithful resolution comparisons gives the equivariant exchange, and pasting follows from the pasting clause of [F1] because both sides are canonically determined by the ordinary pasting squares. This completes claim 2. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, step 3.2]

5.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 prove claims 1 to 3. Every comparison is induced by the ordinary coherent structure of [F1] and the normalization of step 3.2; no unnormalized dualizing shift and no unproved base-change identity is introduced. items.title: General linear Stiefel perverse normalization is exact and conservative
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the finite general
linear Stiefel resolution
$P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N=P_N/G$ of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]
for $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ acting on the separated
finite-type complex variety $X$, with base $B_N$, frame space $U_N$,
$u_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}U_N$, $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$ and
$s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N=u_N-g$. Write $Q_N$ for the finite-resolution functor
and let $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$, $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ be the two
projections. Then:

1. the middle-perverse t-structure on $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is detected by
   restriction to $X$: for every sufficiently large $N$ and every $a$,
   $A\in{}^pD_G^{\le a}$ holds if and only if the restriction of $A$ to $X$
   lies in ${}^pD^{\le a}(X;k)$, if and only if $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ lies in
   ${}^pD^{\le a}(X_N;k)$, and independently of the sufficiently large $N$;
2. the functor $A\mapsto Q_N(A)[s_N]$ is exact for these middle-perverse
   t-structures and conservative in the sense that $Q_N(A)=0$ if and only if
   $A=0$;
3. perverse truncations lift: for $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ and all sufficiently
   large $N$ there is an equivariant perverse truncation
   ${}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A$ with
   $Q_N({}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A)[s_N]\cong{}^p\tau^{\le a}\bigl(Q_N(A)[s_N]\bigr)$,
   canonical up to unique isomorphism, and the family is independent of $N$;
4. at the degree-zero Hom stabilization bound $r_N\ge a-b$ for objects
   concentrated in ordinary degrees $[b,a]$, the ring comparison
   $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ lifts finite
   families of orthogonal idempotents, and after the common shift $s_N$ the
   normalized functor preserves and reflects perverse concentration and
   simplicity.
items.strategy:
1.1 **The dimension correction.** The projections $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$ and $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ are smooth surjective algebraic maps of pure relative complex dimensions $u_N$ and $g$, and $\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X\cong q_N^*Q_N(A)$ by [F3]. Since $s_N+g=u_N$, this gives $q_N^*(Q_N(A)[s_N])[g]\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X[u_N]$. The left side is the normalized object under the perverse-exact functor $q_N^*[g]$, and the right side is $A_X$ under the perverse-exact functor $\operatorname{pr}_X^*[u_N]$. Thus the comparison uses the unshifted base object $A_X$, without an extra shift by $u_N$ on $X$. [F1, F3, given]

1.2 **Connected fibres and local systems.** Each $\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ is path connected: Gaussian elimination expresses an invertible matrix as a product of elementary matrices and nonzero diagonal matrices, each joined to the identity by a path. Each frame space $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$ is the continuous image of connected $\operatorname{GL}_{N_i}(\mathbb C)$ under its first-$n_i$-columns map, so $U_N$ is connected. A locally trivial bundle with connected fibre induces a surjection on fundamental groups: lift a base loop locally and join its endpoint to its initial point inside the fibre. Thus on a connected smooth invariant stratum $S$ both $q_N:U_N\times S\to S_N$ and $\operatorname{pr}_S:U_N\times S\to S$ induce surjective fundamental-group maps. Local trivializations define parallel transport by subdivision along paths; subdivision of a homotopy square proves homotopy invariance, and a sub-local-system is exactly a subspace of one stalk invariant under this loop transport, extended to all stalks by transport. Thus these pullbacks preserve and reflect irreducibility, since the full monodromy image is unchanged. If $L$ is an equivariant local system and $L_N=Q_NL$, any ordinary sub-local-system $M_N\subset L_N$ pulls back to a sub-local-system of $\operatorname{pr}_S^*L$. On the product the $U_N$ factor acts trivially on this monodromy representation and its subrepresentations, so $q_N^*M_N=\operatorname{pr}_S^*M$ for a local system $M$ on $S$. The actual resolution-image criterion in ordinary interval $[0,0]$ descends $M_N$ to an equivariant local system and the degree-zero Hom comparison lifts its injection. Hence $L$ is simple equivariantly if and only if $L_N$ is irreducible ordinarily, and by the connected-fibre pullbacks if and only if its underlying local system on $S$ is irreducible. [F3, F4, given]

2.1 **Detection via restriction to $X$.** By [F1] the shifted pullbacks $\operatorname{pr}_X^*[u_N]$ and $q_N^*[g]$ are exact for the ordinary middle-perverse t-structures and commute with truncation; hence, for every $a$, $q_N^*\bigl(Q_N(A)[s_N]\bigr)[g]=\operatorname{pr}_X^*(A_X[u_N])$ lies in the perverse aisle ${}^pD^{\le a}$ of $P_N$ if and only if $A_X$ lies in ${}^pD^{\le a}$ of $X$, and by exactness of $q_N^*[g]$ this is equivalent to $Q_N(A)[s_N]\in{}^pD^{\le a}(X_N)$. The same computation for the dual aisle identifies the two inequalities, so the structure is detected by restriction to $X$ and by the normalized resolution simultaneously. Independence of the sufficiently large $N$ follows because the conditions are those of the fixed ordinary object $A_X$. This proves claim 1. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **Lift the truncation triangle.** Fix an arbitrary perverse cutoff $c$, and write $A_X$ for restriction of $A$. Let $T_N={}^p\tau^{\le c}(Q_N(A)[s_N])$ and $V_N={}^p\tau^{\ge c+1}(Q_N(A)[s_N])$. The ordinary perverse-exact smooth pullbacks [F1] give $q_N^*T_N\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*({}^p\tau^{\le c}A_X)[s_N]$ and $q_N^*V_N\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*({}^p\tau^{\ge c+1}A_X)[s_N]$. Since the two unshifted pullbacks are exact and conservative, the ordinary amplitudes of $T_N[-s_N]$ and $V_N[-s_N]$ equal those of the two ordinary truncations on $X$, independently of $N$. Choose one interval containing these amplitudes and that of $A$, enlarge it to include cones of the triangle arrows, and choose $r_N$ larger than its width. The image criterion [F3] lifts the two unshifted truncations, and degree-zero full faithfulness lifts their arrows to and from $A$. Complete the lifted first arrow to a distinguished triangle; exactness of $Q_N$ and full faithfulness identify its cone and connecting map with $V_N[-s_N]$ and its connecting map. Thus the whole truncation triangle lifts. On $X$ its outer objects lie in the desired two perverse aisles, by step 2.1. No arbitrary ordinary perverse object is assumed to descend. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The perverse structure, uniqueness and conservativity.** Define the two equivariant aisles by ordinary restriction. Their shift closures are inherited from [F2]. For objects in opposite aisles, choose a single sufficiently large resolution for their ordinary amplitudes; step 2.1 places their normalized images in opposite ordinary perverse aisles, and the faithful degree-zero Hom comparison [F3] gives orthogonality. Step 3.1 supplies truncation triangles, so these aisles form a bounded t-structure. The usual truncation uniqueness follows from orthogonality: a map from an object in the lower aisle to $A$ factors uniquely through the lower truncation, as the Hom groups to the upper term and its $[-1]$ shift vanish. Consequently the lifts are canonical up to unique isomorphism and agree for different sufficiently large $N$. Step 2.1 makes $Q_N(-)[s_N]$ perverse exact. Finally, $Q_N(A)=0$ implies $\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X=q_N^*Q_N(A)=0$; surjective exact $\operatorname{pr}_X^*$ gives $A_X=0$, and conservative restriction [F3] gives $A=0$. This proves claims 1–3, without applying a Hom bound to an arbitrary fixed small $N$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1]

4.2 **Projectors, concentration and simplicity.** Let $K\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ have ordinary cohomology in $[b,a]$ with $a-b\le r_N$, so that the degree-zero ring comparison $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ of [F3] is an isomorphism. A finite family of mutually orthogonal idempotents in $\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ summing to the identity pulls back to a finite family in $\operatorname{End}_G(K)$ with the same relations, and the idempotent splitting of [F3] splits each of them; the summands remain in $[b,a]$ because ordinary cohomology of a direct summand is a direct summand. By claims 1 and 2 the normalized functor is exact and conservative, so a nonzero proper equivariant subobject of a lift would give a nonzero proper ordinary subobject of the corresponding normalized object; this proves reflection of simplicity, which is the direction consumed by the semisimplicity application, as well as detection of perverse concentration. The preservation direction is proved below using the actual connected general linear group hypothesis and local-system descent. This proves claim 4. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Underlying ordinary simplicity.** The equivariant truncations of step 3.1 and the localization adjunctions of [F4] define intermediate extension by the image of ${}^pH^0j_!\to{}^pH^0Rj_*$. A simple equivariant heart object $A$ has irreducible invariant support $Z$: the finite support components are permuted by connected $G$, hence individually invariant, and localization on a dense component would otherwise yield a nonzero proper subobject. Choose the invariant dense smooth open where its ordinary cohomology is locally constant; equivariance preserves this locus and algebraic constructibility gives a dense algebraic such open. The perverse inequalities force restriction there to be a local system $L[\dim Z]$. A proper equivariant sub-local-system yields a proper subobject by localization adjunction and perverse image, so $L$ is simple equivariantly. Absence of boundary subobjects and quotients identifies $A$ with $j_{!*}L[\dim Z]$ by the image and adjunction characterization of [F2]. Restriction is perverse exact by step 2.1 and commutes with localization in [F4], hence with that image. Step 1.2 makes $L$ irreducible ordinarily, so $A_X$ is the ordinary simple intersection complex of [F2]. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 1.2]

6.1 **Preservation after normalization.** Smooth dimension-shifted pullback along a locally trivial map with connected smooth fibres preserves ordinary simple intersection complexes: the fundamental-group surjection preserves irreducibility on the dense smooth open, smooth local product comparison commutes with $j_!$ and $Rj_*$ on boundary charts, and perverse exactness carries their intermediate-extension image to the same image upstairs. Here the fibres are irreducible frame spaces, so the inverse image of an irreducible support is irreducible. Apply this to $\operatorname{pr}_X$, with fibre $U_N$. For simple equivariant $A$, step 5.1 makes $A_X$ simple, so $\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X[u_N]$ is simple. By step 1.1 this is $q_N^*(Q_N(A)[s_N])[g]$. Any nonzero proper subobject of $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ would give one upstairs through exact conservative $q_N^*[g]$, a contradiction. Thus normalization preserves simplicity; reflection is step 4.2 and concentration is step 2.1. Both directions use the same $s_N=u_N-g$ and stated ring-comparison threshold, with the actual product of connected general linear groups. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.2, step 5.1]

7.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 prove claims 1–3, and steps 4.2, 5.1 and 6.1 claim 4. The dimension shift is $s_N=u_N-g=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N$, not $u_N$ and not $g$; no arbitrary perverse object on $X_N$ is asserted to descend, and no derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is used. AC enters as recorded in [A1]. [given, A1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: Middle perverse t structure glues and has simple intersection complexes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero. On the equivariant constructible derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]],
middle perversity is tested on the ordinary restriction $A_X$ and its
smooth complex constructibility strata $S$ by the two
inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A_X)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and
$H^q(i_S^!A_X)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$, where $i_S$ is the inclusion of a
stratum. These inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of
compatible refinement and gluing across $G$-invariant algebraic open/closed
decompositions, and the perverse aisles are detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is
abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate
extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=i_{Z*}j_{!*}(L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z])$ of simple
finite-rank local systems $L$ on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports
$Z$, where $Z$ and the dense open are $G$-invariant, $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$
is the closed inclusion, $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is the dense open inclusion,
and $L$ has equivariant data. If $A,B$ lie in the
heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's
endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.
items.strategy:
1.1 **The equivariant t-structure.** For $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ define $A\in{}^pD_G^{\le a}$ if and only if the restriction $A_X$ lies in the ordinary aisle ${}^pD^{\le a}(X;k)$, and ${}^pD_G^{\ge a}$ dually. By [F1] this is equivalent to $Q_N(A)[s_N]\in{}^pD^{\le a}(X_N;k)$ for every sufficiently large $N$, so the definition is independent of the resolution. The pair $({}^pD_G^{\le0},{}^pD_G^{\ge0})$ satisfies the t-structure axioms because the defining conditions are those of a t-structure pointwise: closure under shifts and extensions follows from the corresponding ordinary closures and the conservativity of restriction, orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}({}^pD_G^{\le0},{}^pD_G^{\ge1})=0$ follows from the ordinary orthogonality transported through the fully faithful Hom comparison of [F1], and truncation triangles exist by the lifting clause of [F1]. The structure is bounded because the ordinary one is and restriction to $X$ is conservative. This proves the t-structure and detection assertions. [F1, F3, given]

2.1 **Gluing and independence of refinement.** The inequalities of the Statement are checked stratumwise and are therefore independent of compatible refinement by the ordinary clause of [F3]; gluing across an algebraic open/closed decomposition uses the localization triangles of [F2] and the ordinary gluing theorem: for a $G$-invariant open immersion $j$ and its closed complement $i$, the Čech-style recollement conditions $j^*i_*=0$, the triangles $j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}\to i_*i^*$ and $i_*i^!\to\mathrm{id}\to j_*j^*$ hold in $D^b_{G,c}$ by [F2], and the transport of step 1.1 reduces the glued t-structure statement to the ordinary one. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 **Heart and finite length.** Kernel and cokernel of a morphism of the heart are the perverse cohomology objects in degrees $-1$ and $0$ of its cone, computed by the truncation functors of step 1.1; hence the heart is abelian. Restriction to $X$ is perverse exact and conservative on the heart by [F1], so a strictly increasing or decreasing chain of subobjects in the equivariant heart gives a strictly increasing or decreasing chain in the ordinary heart; the ordinary heart has finite length by [F3], so the equivariant heart does. For heart objects $A,B$ and $m<0$, $B[m]$ lies in ${}^pD_G^{\ge1}$ while $A$ lies in ${}^pD_G^{\le0}$, so orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **Intersection complexes and simples.** Let $Z$ be an irreducible invariant support, let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an invariant dense smooth open of dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}Z$, and let $L$ be a simple equivariant local system on $U$. The perverse input is $P=L[d]$, and define $j_{!*}P=\operatorname{im}({}^pH^0j_!P\to{}^pH^0Rj_*P)$ and $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=i_{Z*}j_{!*}P$. The localization adjunctions [F2] identify the largest boundary quotient of a heart object $E$ with ${}^pH^0i_*i^*E$ and the largest boundary subobject with ${}^pH^0i_*i^!E$. Applied to this image, these are zero; conversely the two adjunction maps identify an extension with this image whenever it has neither boundary subobjects nor boundary quotients. If $L$ is simple, a subobject of its intermediate extension either restricts to zero, hence is a forbidden boundary subobject, or restricts to all of $P$, leaving a forbidden boundary quotient. Thus the intersection complex is simple. For a simple equivariant heart object, the underlying simplicity clause of [F1] gives irreducible support and an irreducible local system on its dense smooth local-system locus. Connected $G$ preserves this intrinsic locus and each irreducible support component, so the support and a dense algebraic local-system open are invariant. Localization supplies the equivariant local system there, and the absence of boundary subobjects and quotients identifies the object with $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)$. This proves both directions using the shifted heart input, rather than taking perverse degree zero of the unshifted local system. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.2]

4.1 **Endomorphism rings.** Let $S$ be a simple heart object and $f:S\to S$ a nonzero endomorphism. Its kernel is a subobject of $S$ and hence zero, and its image is a nonzero subobject and hence all of $S$; thus $f$ is invertible. Therefore $\operatorname{End}(S)$ is a division $k$-algebra, and it is not asserted to equal $k$. This completes the proof. [F3, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the t-structure, its independence of refinement and gluing; steps 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1 give the heart, its finite length, the negative-Hom vanishing and the intersection-complex classification with division endomorphism rings. AC enters as recorded in [A1], and no semisimplicity or characteristic restriction beyond characteristic zero is used. [given, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: Equivariant constructible Ext is degreewise finite and compatible with characteristic zero scalars
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex
algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero. For
bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the equivariant category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]:

1. every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ is
   finite-dimensional over $k$ and vanishes for all sufficiently negative $m$;
2. for every field extension $k\to K$ of characteristic-zero fields, the
   canonical map
   $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$
   is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and
   with Yoneda composition;
3. coefficient extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized
   Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these
   bounded constructible objects.

The total Ext space $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ need not be
finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under
coefficient extension.
items.strategy:
1.1 **Finiteness and vanishing.** Let $A,B$ be bounded constructible with $A\le a$ and $B\ge b$, fix $m$, and let $I$ be an ordinary cohomological interval containing the amplitudes of $A$ and of $B[m]$. Choose $N_i\ge n_i+1$ with $r_N\ge\operatorname{length}(I)$; such a choice is possible because $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$ grows without bound with the $N_i$. By [F1] there is a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$, and by [F2] the right-hand side is computed by a bounded finite-dimensional cochain model on the finite-type variety $X_N$, hence is finite-dimensional. If $b-a>m$, then $B[m]\ge b-m>a$ and the ordinary t-structure orthogonality makes $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<b-a$, so the groups vanish for sufficiently negative $m$. This proves claim 1. [F1, F2, F5]

1.2 **Scalar extension.** Coefficient extension on the simplicial category is termwise tensor with $K$, hence exact by [F4], and it commutes with inverse image and with the free-quotient descent used to define $Q_N$ because those constructions are given locally by exact inverse image along algebraic sections together with gluing. Therefore $Q_N(A_K)\cong(Q_N(A))_K$ and $Q_N(B_K)\cong(Q_N(B))_K$, and the same $N$ works over $k$ and over $K$: the fiber-gap vanishing of [F1] is field-independent and the finite models of [F2] commute with coefficient extension, so the interval bookkeeping is unchanged. In the resulting commutative square of Hom comparisons the vertical arrows are the full-faithfulness isomorphisms of [F1] over $k$ and over $K$, and the bottom horizontal arrow is the ordinary bounded constructible Hom coefficient-extension isomorphism of [F2]; hence the top horizontal arrow, which is the canonical map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$, is an isomorphism. Naturality in $A$ and $B$ and compatibility with shifts hold because all maps are induced by functors and by the termwise base change, and compatibility with Yoneda composition holds because the comparisons are induced by functors and one sufficiently large $N$ serves the finitely many composable classes of a Yoneda product. No infinite totalization or infinite product of injectives is tensored with $K$. This proves claim 2. [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 **Commutation with the operations and the perverse structure.** The ordinary coherent six operations and normalized Verdier duality are determined on the finite constructible models of [F2], and the ordinary coefficient-extension clause of [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] shows that termwise exact coefficient extension commutes with inverse image, finite cochain pushforward, tensor, internal Hom and the finite-dimensional duality comparisons of [F3]; transporting through the finite-resolution comparisons as in step 1.2 gives the commutation with the equivariant operations and with normalized duality. For the perverse structure, exact coefficient extension preserves the upper support inequalities on ordinary restriction. It also preserves the lower inequalities, since it commutes with ordinary Verdier duality and that duality exchanges the two aisles. Hence it is perverse t-exact in the equivariant category detected by restriction [F3]. Applying it to a truncation triangle gives the unique truncation triangle over $K$, so perverse truncations and cohomology commute with extension. Its induced functor on the abelian hearts is exact and therefore preserves the image defining $j_{!*}$; the already proved commutation with $j_!$ and $Rj_*$ gives intermediate-extension commutation. This proves claim 3. Simplicity under extension is deliberately not asserted: a simple local system may fail to remain simple after extending scalars. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2]

3.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 prove claims 1 to 3. The proof is finite-stage: one sufficiently large resolution handles a fixed bounded object and its finitely many shifted targets, and no infinite-dimensional total Ext space is used. The total Ext space is not claimed to be finite, and simplicity is not claimed to be preserved. AC enters as recorded in [A1]. [given, A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Equivariant Ext of a point is degreewise finite and not total finite
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let
$G=\mathbb C^\times=\operatorname{GL}_1(\mathbb C)$ act trivially on the point
$X=\operatorname{pt}$, in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Let $k$ be a
field of characteristic zero and let $k$ also denote the constant equivariant
object. Then
$$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)\cong\begin{cases}k,&m\ge0\text{ even},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Hence the Ext groups are degreewise finite-dimensional but their total direct
sum $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)$ is infinite-dimensional. The
forgetful restriction to the ordinary point is not derived fully faithful.
